problems.title: Combine two remainder conditions
problems.question: a leaves remainder 3 modulo 6 and 1 modulo 4. Find its remainder modulo 12.
problems.idea: Check the two residues compatible with the first condition.
steps: Of these, only 9 leaves remainder 1 modulo 4.

problems.title: Only the two middle gaps are shaded
problems.question: Two tangent unit circles fit side by side in a rectangle. Find the shaded upper and lower gaps between them.
problems.idea: Use the central rectangle between the circle centres.
formulas: Central rectangle area=2·2; two semicircle areas=π.
steps: The shaded gaps lie in the width-2 central strip.
The portions of the circles in that strip are two semicircles of total area π.
problems.note: The four outer corner gaps are not shaded; including them would give a different area.

problems.title: Apply the recurrence in order
problems.question: b₁=-1,b₂=2,bₙ₊₂=bₙ²-2bₙ₊₁. Find b₅.
problems.idea: Each new term uses the previous two.

problems.title: A two-step increase in a geometric progression
problems.question: In a positive geometric progression, b₉ is 21% greater than b₇. Find the common ratio.
problems.idea: Two steps multiply a term by r².
steps: All terms are positive, so r is positive.

problems.title: Opposite side sums identify an incircle
problems.question: The quadrilateral’s side lengths a,b,d,c in that order form an arithmetic progression; in the diagram a,c are opposite and b,d are opposite. What must hold?
problems.idea: Express the progression with a first term and difference.
steps: By the converse of Pitot’s theorem for a convex quadrilateral, equal opposite-side sums imply that the quadrilateral has an incircle.
Thus it is circumscribed about a circle.

problems.title: Three expressions in arithmetic progression
problems.question: Find the least x for which x²-4,5x+3,3x+2 form an arithmetic progression in that order.
problems.idea: The middle term is the average of its neighbours.

problems.title: Sum an arithmetic progression
problems.question: Find 9+19+29+…+189+199.
problems.idea: Count the terms and average the endpoints.

problems.title: A mean determines the common difference
problems.question: The mean of the first n terms of an arithmetic progression equals n for every positive integer n. Find its difference.
problems.idea: Use n=1 and n=2.
steps: Then the mean formula indeed equals n for all n.

problems.title: Recover a term from partial sums
problems.question: Sₙ=6((-1/2)ⁿ-1). Find 12b₃.
problems.idea: Subtract consecutive partial sums.

problems.title: A right triangle in geometric progression
problems.question: The sides of a right triangle form a geometric progression. Find hypotenuse/shorter leg.
problems.idea: Write the increasing side lengths as a,ar,ar².

problems.title: A nonnegative modular representative
problems.question: Find the least nonnegative residue of -26 modulo 6.
problems.idea: Add a multiple of 6 to enter [0,6).
steps: The remainder is 4, which lies from 0 through 5.

problems.title: A complex rational inequality
problems.question: Solve (1/(x-1)-1)/(1-1/(x-7))>0.
problems.idea: Record all restrictions before clearing the smaller fractions.
steps: A sign chart gives a positive value on (1,2) and (7,8), and a negative value elsewhere.
Every endpoint is excluded: 2 makes the quotient zero, and the others are forbidden.

problems.title: A vector to a point on a parallel section
problems.question: M∈AB,N∈AC,MN∥BC,MN:BC=2:3. Given AB=a,BC=b as vectors, find 6BN.
problems.idea: Similarity gives AN as a fraction of AC.

problems.title: Every angle must be acute
problems.question: For which a is the angle between m=(x,a),n=(x-a,1) acute for every real x?
problems.idea: A positive dot product is the acute-angle condition.
steps: This quadratic is strictly positive for all x exactly when a-a²/4>0.
For these parameters neither vector can be zero.

problems.title: Traverse a regular hexagon with vectors
problems.question: In regular ABCDEF, AB=n,AF=m. Express DF.
problems.idea: Use the three repeating edge directions.
steps: Taking A as origin gives D=2n+2m and F=m.

problems.title: Angle from components
problems.question: Find the cosine between m=3i-4j and n=5i+12j in standard Cartesian coordinates.
problems.idea: Use their dot product and lengths.
problems.note: This uses the usual orthonormal coordinate vectors i,j. An arbitrary non-orthonormal basis would require its lengths and mutual angle.

problems.title: Equal sum and difference lengths
problems.question: What follows necessarily from |a-b|=|a+b|?
problems.idea: Square and expand both sides.
steps: For nonzero vectors this also means a⊥b.
Neither individual length must be zero or equal to the other.
problems.answer: a·b=0; for nonzero vectors, a⊥b as well.
problems.note: Two printed choices, perpendicular vectors and zero dot product, express the same conclusion for nonzero vectors. If zero vectors are allowed, the dot-product statement remains unambiguous.

problems.title: A geometric series cancels a sine square
problems.question: Evaluate sin²15°(1/(1+cos15°)+1+cos15°+cos²15°+…).
problems.idea: Sum the geometric series with ratio c=cos15°.

problems.title: Compare an infinite sum with its first two terms
problems.question: A positive decreasing geometric series has total sum 1.8 times the sum of its first two terms. Find its ratio.
problems.idea: Cancel the positive first term.
steps: So r²=4/9 and positivity selects r=2/3.

problems.title: Equilateral triangle from a radius difference
problems.question: An equilateral triangle has circumradius minus inradius equal to 1. Find its area.
problems.idea: The circumradius is twice the inradius.

problems.title: Integer angles in a convex dodecagon
problems.question: The interior angles of a convex 12-gon are increasing positive integers in arithmetic progression. Maximize the smallest angle.
problems.idea: Use the angle sum and the smallest possible common difference.
steps: Since the angles are integers, d is a positive integer. The equation forces d to be even.
The least possible difference is d=2°, giving a₁=150°-11°=139°.
The largest angle is then 161°, below 180°, so the convex-angle requirement is satisfied.

problems.title: Diagonals of an isosceles trapezoid
problems.question: In isosceles OMNK, O=(0,0),K=(8,0),N=(5,4), and the bases are horizontal. Find the cosine of the acute angle between diagonals.
problems.idea: Symmetry locates M=(3,4).

problems.title: Length of a linear combination
problems.question: |a|=2,|b|=1 and their angle is 120°. Find |2a+3b|.
problems.idea: Expand the squared length.

problems.title: Angle between two rectangle diagonals
problems.question: The pictured congruent rectangles ABCD and MBNK have sides 2,6. Find cos∠ACK.
problems.idea: Choose coordinates at their common corner B.

problems.title: Two simultaneous congruences
problems.question: Solve x≡3 (mod 5), x≡1 (mod 8).
problems.idea: Write the second condition as x=1+8k.
steps: Thus k=4+5t and x=33+40t for an integer t.
